reviews.brief_observed_notes: Correct D. Appropriate instability/positive FAST/peritonitis logic, with explicit reliance on standard teaching and truncated excerpts. One cited view states FAST can identify fluid in unstable patients; the other only states a study objective, so claiming an established operative association exceeds that visible excerpt. WSES independently supports the option but does not repair the partial original citation.

Correct C. Substantively broadens an empty multihormone query, then actually reads two found studies. The 76-patient CHF abstract directly reports higher BNP/ADH/renin-aldosterone activity with hyponatremia; the copeptin cohort addresses biomarkers/prognosis rather than every laboratory mechanism. Explicitly separates inferred potassium from source measurements.

Correct D. Substantively broadens a restrictive first search and distinguishes the proximal facilitation/autonomic pattern from MG. The registered excerpts support presynaptic P/Q pathology and LEMS phenotype; the SCLC frequency and specific anticholinesterase response are not visible in these two cited snippets.

Correct B. Correctly distinguishes primary prophase-I arrest, later meiosis-I completion around ovulation and metaphase-II arrest until fertilization. The extra approximate gestational timing is not source-verified; its knowledge-only provenance is explicit.

Correct B, but says the 20,536-person randomized trial confirmed a liver-enzyme association when its delivered excerpt contains background/methods only. The independent full abstract instead reports no significant serious hepatobiliary difference and undetectable hepatitis risk; it does not quantify all mild elevations. Also calls metformin non-hepatotoxic absolutely despite rare documented injury. The real simvastatin case supports the central adverse-effect option, without rescuing these overstatements.

Correct D. Connects the supplied chronic renal framing, azotemia/hyperkalemia and pericarditic findings to broad/waxy casts, with appropriate acute/glomerular/nephrotic distractors. Explicitly acknowledges the empty search and knowledge-only basis.

Correct D. Coherent perfusion/ischemia reasoning, with a burn-flow statement directly present in a rat paper background and early-local-ischemia wording in the review. The human hemodynamic search excerpt gives methods, not measured results; all three are cited without reading. Species/read-extent limits constrain clinical corroboration.

Correct B. Direct excerpts support OA symptoms and obesity as a major modifiable risk factor, while OSA/diabetes associations are explicitly left as existing knowledge. Does not claim that OA papers independently verify all comorbidities or this individual diagnosis.

Correct C. Uses familial echinocytic anemia and distinguishes PFK-1 regulation from the deficient pyruvate kinase enzyme. Explicitly labels the indirect PKA/F2,6BP mechanism as hepatic, avoiding a direct red-cell PFK-1 phosphorylation claim. Knowledge-only provenance is stated; Rider independently supports the biochemical distinction.

Correct C. Integrates gluten timing, failed dairy withdrawal, serologies and the malabsorptive/rash phenotype with classic villous atrophy/crypt hyperplasia. Distinguishes the provided hypertrophy wording from standard hyperplasia terminology. Explicitly acknowledges no retrieved verification.

Correct C. Actually reads found serologic studies; accurately attributes acute HBsAg/IgM markers and high acute anti-HBc IgM. The quantitative source also shows positive/high IgM in chronic carriers with flares, so these data cannot prove exclusive acute specificity. It does not claim the numerical cutoff is universally diagnostic or adopt the old review treatment advice. The indexed quantitative abstract itself carries a 250-word truncation notice despite the transport flag.

Correct D. Broadens the initial full-symptom/dry-tap query and retrieves direct HCL/TRAP descriptions. Correctly notes that dry-tap fibrosis is not discussed by its snippets instead of claiming source verification of every vignette feature.

Correct C. Actual excerpt supports travel-associated fever, splenomegaly and rose spots, but calling the rash pathognomonic overstates specificity and presence; the same excerpt reports rose spots in only 11 percent. It also dismisses schistosomiasis as exclusively chronic despite CDC acute presentations. These explanatory limitations do not reassign the released key.

Correct D. Appropriate palpable-testis surgery/distractor interpretation at eleven months. Actual snippets explicitly give both the 6-18-month interval and the more precise 6-12 goal/no-later-than-18 upper bound. It does not claim direct full-guideline reading or a measured cancer-risk effect size.

Correct D. Gives standard CTZ/D2 versus competing-pathway rationale and explicitly leaves the specific AP localization to existing pharmacology. The two excerpts support multifactorial emesis/transmitter background rather than all central CINV receptor/site details claimed. REGLAN researcher context does not become retroactive retrieved evidence.

Correct A. Broadens the initial criteria-heavy query and actually reads old treatment/audit abstracts with explicit doxycycline options. The indication is based on the vignette triad; the 2004 guideline has additional risk criteria not explicitly met by this 53-year-old with FEV1 57 percent, so it cannot alone verify the patient-level rule. Local severity/resistance/culture limits are acknowledged.

Correct antidote and clinically coherent perioperative differential. Specific anesthetic exposure is inferred; both cited search excerpts support the MH phenotype/trigger but neither delivered excerpt reaches a dantrolene recommendation. The model acknowledges truncation and does not invent a dose.

Correct tinea cruris from groin/perineal distribution and scrotal sparing, with knowledge provenance stated. Describing balanitis as characteristically scrotal conflates glans inflammation with intertrigo; this is a minor distractor explanation issue.

Correct neural-tube-defect selection. Actually read the 1992 review explicitly reporting a 1% spina-bifida association with carbamazepine; the estimate is properly attributed to an older review rather than presented as a current guideline estimate.

Released-key mismatch: selects contrast enema before any initial radiograph is provided. The read imaging review explicitly places radiography before classifying obstruction; the other reads support enema therapy once uncomplicated meconium ileus is established. Relevant retrieval does not establish that this distressed infant has already reached that stage.

Matches the released xanthine-oxidase key and correctly presents azathioprine treatment as a possibility rather than a supplied fact. Delivered excerpt explicitly verifies the drug-class/thiopurine interaction and myelosuppression; patient-specific exposure remains unconfirmed.
Correct incretin-preservation mechanism and clear contrasts with sulfonylurea, SGLT2 and PPAR-gamma options; no tool evidence claimed or fabricated.

Correct GM-CSF selection with accurate ANC calculation (280/mm3). Three searches do not find direct reaction evidence, and the model appropriately declines to cite the unrelated medulloblastoma excerpt. Official label independently supports first-administration respiratory/hemodynamic reaction.

Correct hypothyroid phenotype and TSH finding. The diagnosis/TSH excerpt is useful, whereas the second cited opening defines etiologies rather than verifying the whole symptom complex or hyper-to-hypothyroid course.

Correct XLA presentation and plausible contrasts with ataxia-telangiectasia/DiGeorge/T-cell disorders. Citation scope is accurately limited to B-cell defects and respiratory infections; the age/pathogen detail is not falsely represented as present in excerpts.

Correct translocation with accurate SAAG 1.8 and PMNs 1140; explicitly notes missing cultures. Actual SBP review directly supplies altered host defenses and gut translocation. The second cited study concerns non-neutrocytic ascites, giving indirect mechanistic context rather than confirming this episode.

Correct fragile-X option with two pertinent excerpts, one supplying the repeat expansion and both the long-face/prominent-ear phenotype. No unsupported numerical prevalence or patient-specific genetic confirmation is added.

Matches the key and recognizes the new antiemetic temporal clue as possible dopamine-blocker NMS, rather than declaring a particular party drug. Does not falsely cite the MDMA/MH hits as NMS management evidence. Dantrolene as an adjunct here is clinical knowledge, not comparative efficacy established by the Reglan label.

Correct lamotrigine with a fitting early severe-cutaneous-reaction suspicion. Calls the vignette mucocutaneous SJS despite no mucosal findings being supplied; the 2-8-week risk is label-supported researcher context, not delivered by either short excerpt. The prevention excerpt lists AEDs as a class, not lamotrigine by name in its body.

Correct sympathetic activation and vagal withdrawal, with an explicit baroreflex-reset qualification. Fits the systolic/heart-rate rise with little diastolic change; no retrieved mechanism or comparative experiment is claimed.
